MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 25, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on September 25, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 20, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:03 p.m.)
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Sachs declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:01
p.m. with all five City Council Members present

INVOCATION: Mayor Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

City Council Minutes  1  September 25, 2018
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Sachs presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Kimmi Le and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Corporal Ryan
  McShefferey.

P2.  Moulton Niguel Water District Thanks City of Mission Viejo for its Partnership - 50
  Years of Water Recycling

  The City Council received the presentation from Matt Collings, Moulton Niguel Water
  District Assistant General Manager, on behalf of the MNWD Board of Directors.

P3.  Proclaim October 7 through 13, 2018 To Be "Fire Prevention Week"

  Mayor Sachs issued the proclamation to Orange County Fire Authority Chief Rob
  Capobianco.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ryan Farsai, M.V.: discussed his ongoing dispute with the City regarding property rights at 25122
Marguerite Parkway and the pending liquor license for the ARCO station he co-owns.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of September 11, 2018, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated August 31, 2018 in the Amount of $1,029,639.95

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated September 7, 2018 in the Amount of $223,909.77

  Ratified the accompanying check register.
City Council Minutes  2  September 25, 2018
 4.  Contract Amendment—Siemens Mobility, Inc.

  Approved First Amendment to Contract with Siemens Industry, Inc., to reflect the change
  of the company's name to Siemens Mobility, Inc.

5.  Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 18837)–
  Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

6.  Curb Address Number Painting, Southerly Section (CIP 18836)—Notice of
  Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

7.  Los Alisos Boulevard Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (Project P)
  Cooperative Agreement

  Approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-8-1799 with the Orange County Transportation
  Authority for the Los Alisos Boulevard Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Project
  (CIP 19240).

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARINGS

8.  Felipe Tennis and Recreation Center Facility Regulations and Facility Rental Rates

  Community Services Manager Lydie Gutfeld presented the staff report.

  Mayor Sachs opened the public hearing at 6:30 p.m. With no requests to speak from
  members of the public, Mayor Sachs closed the public hearing.

City Council Minutes  3  September 25, 2018
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  approve the recommended facility regulations and room/facility rental rates for the Felipe
  Tennis and Recreation Center.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

9.  Cost Recovery Policies

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to adopt
  Resolution 18-41 Approving Council Policy 0300-11 - Cost Recovery Policies.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

10.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum deferred the report to the next meeting.

11.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Sachs announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the OCFA Board and
  he deferred the report.

STAFF REPORTS

12.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update from Chief Capobianco

  Chief Capobianco discussed OCFA’s agreement that will allow for use of SDG&E’s new
  helitanker during wildfires. The helitanker can drop 2,600 gallons of water and will be
  available to south Orange County. He discussed recent department promotions and the Fire
  Captain and Engineers Academies. Chief Capobianco noted that OCFA’s Urban Search
  and Rescue (USAR) Team responded to Hurricane Florence where five members from
  Station 9 assisted the City of Beulaville with deployment and 7 rescues. He also announced
  that OCFA’s 2018 Open House programs will be held on October 6, 2018 from 10:00 a.m.
City Council Minutes  4  September 25, 2018
   to 3:00 p.m. at OCFA Headquarters and October 13 from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at
  participating fire stations throughout the County.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she was honored to be elected as the District 13
representative on the Orange County Council of Governments (OCCOG) Board. She said OCCOG
works with the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) on regional issues and
she thanked her colleagues for attending the meeting and voting for her. Council Member
Bucknum discussed her participation in Innercoastal Cleanup Day and observed that since then,
she has seen people picking up trash while they are out walking around town. She encouraged
residents to clean up after themselves and keep trash out of the creek and waterways. Council
Member Bucknum noted that election season has begun and campaign signs are beginning to
appear. Mission Viejo has designated corners where candidates are allowed to place signs and she
wanted to make residents aware that they are permitted in certain locations. She discussed
upcoming events in the busy month of October which include Pumpkin Diving, the 30th Annual
Walk Against Drugs, the DAWG Walk and Pet Faire and a rock concert called Roctober. In
closing, Council Member Bucknum shared that she is the proud new grandma of a baby girl.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell extended his congratulations to Council Member Bucknum for her
election to the OCCOG Board where she will represent region 13. In that role, she will address
issues concerning transportation, regional housing needs assessments, and other matters that are
very important to the community. Council Member Goodell said it is great to have someone who
is so committed representing Mission Viejo and the region. He also announced that the Mission
Viejo Olympic Promotion Committee had a recent meeting where they discussed ideas for creating
promotional packages to send out to the Olympic Committees’ national governing bodies. He
stated that it’s a great group of people that are excited to promote the City to the best of their
ability. Council Member Goodell discussed the proliferation of dog waste that he has seen recently
and reminded residents to please be respectful and pick up after dogs and throw the bags away. He
said he has also been noticing a lot of cigarette butts on the streets when he's out walking his dogs.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at Mission Viejo Library’s volunteer recognition
event and said it was heartwarming to look out and see a room full of volunteers who give their
time to the Library. She stated that she is mindful of all the money and resources that are saved as
a result of their work and she expressed her appreciation to all of the City's volunteers. Council
City Council Minutes  5  September 25, 2018
 Member Kelley announced that she too participated in Innercoastal Cleanup Day where she saw a
huge group of Scouts, the Mission Viejo Nadadores and many families hard at work. She noted
that it was great to see so many people out there caring about the environment and keeping the city
clean. Council Member Kelley reminded residents of the golf ball drop fundraiser that will benefit
the City's adopted Marines. The October 12 golf tournament is sold out but the Adoption
Committee is still looking for donors to buy golf balls for the drop. She said it is a great way to
support the men and women who are serving the nation. Residents can purchase one ball for $10
or 20 balls for $150. Additional information is available at the Murray Community Center or
people can purchase tickets online at www.teeitupforemarines.com. Council Member Kelley
announced that she will be out of town next week at the National Forum on Character in
Washington, DC, where she’ll present a breakout session on Mission Viejo’s Community of
Character program.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths stated that he was honored to attend the YMCA’s Charity golf tournament
on September 14 at Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club. The event was sponsored by Lexus of Mission
Viejo and Waste Management and he said he appreciates everything the YMCA does for children.
Mayor Pro Tem Raths said that he is looking forward to attending the Mission Viejo High School
“Mission Armed Forces” football game on Friday night to honor veterans and he thanked everyone
who puts that game together. He announced that his 6th grandchild, a girl, arrived a couple hours
ago and he closed by noting the increased visibility and police presence since Chief Vuong took
over. He thanked Orange County Sheriff’s Department and Orange County Fire Authority for all
that they do to keep the community safe.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs noted that he observed a horrific car accident a couple of weeks ago at Jeronimo and
Alicia where one of the cars ended up on its side. Since then, he has seen the prolific running of
red lights around the City so he talked to staff to see if lights can be reconfigured to delay the green
for traffic going the other direction. He said he learned that the City is already doing that and in
addition, the Sheriff’s department monitored two major intersections and in just 2½ hours, motor
officers cited 6 red light violations at Alicia and Jeronimo. The following day in just 1½ hours, 11
citations were written at Oso and Marguerite. Mayor Sachs reminded residents that the City is
paying attention to this and staff will use technology to cut down on some of the potential accidents
due to red light violations. He encouraged residents to take their time and be cautious. Referencing
Chief Capobianco’s report on the teams that deployed to the Carolinas and Virginia to help with
hurricane rescue efforts, Mayor Sachs noted that Orange County Fire Authority personnel drove
to the east coast and immediately started working and they were exhausted. He said he will be
penning a letter to the President of the United States, Homeland Security and others, to request
that aircraft fly the firefighters and their equipment to parts of the country where emergencies exist
so the firefighters can be rested and ready to go.

City Council Minutes  6  September 25, 2018
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:12 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, October 9, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 9, 2018

City Council Minutes  7  September 25, 2018
